content.text:
Looking at the data:
- Core Zone_F3_Z01 (Core_mid) temperature rises relative to other zones starting around week 33–35 (early-mid July 2018), reaching ~25.0–25.3 °C by autumn.
- Cooling setpoint is essentially unchanged (≈25.14 °C), heating setpoint unchanged (≈18.7 °C).
- Core temperature now exceeds the cooling setpoint (e.g., 25.27 °C vs. 25.19 °C CP at wk50), while other zones are trending lower (23–24 °C).
- The building's data store exposes only: zone air temperatures, heating/cooling setpoints. No energy consumption, HVAC valve/actuator, OA/damper, or return-air streams are present.

Either hypothesis (a real local load increase causing the controller to lose, or a sensor drift/fault reading high) produces exactly this pattern with the available signals. Neither set of available streams lets me discriminate them — distinguishing "reported T above CP due to lost control vs. sensor bias" requires a corroborating signal that isn't present.

input.needed_streams: Zone-level electrical/thermal energy consumption for Core_mid (Zone_F3_Z01) (to see if HVAC or internal loads actually increased), the zone cooling valve/actuator position (to see if the controller is already working at max — which would support a real load increase over a sensor fault), outdoor/return-air temperature to rule out a shared supply anomaly, and a redundant/independent zone temperature sensor for Zone_F3_Z01 to compare against the reported one (to detect sensor bias). The current store only has zone air temperature and heating/cooling setpoints, which both candidate causes look identical in (temperature rising above unchanged cooling setpoint while other zones trend the opposite way).
